items.title: Joe Wilder Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: I subbed with them a few times with Boulez was there and when Kostelanetz was there.

ctx.x: You sound like you play a lot better at it today. And you’ve played with the New York Philharmonic?

I subbed with them a few times with Boulez was there and when Kostelanetz was there. And usually there was times when they were doing “The Pines of Rome” and they added a couple of extra trumpets or something.
How about your first big band experience? You’ve played in so many big bands.

items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Kastelanetz, and Jimmy Holmes was – Jimmy Chambers, rather, was the contractor, he called me for a few things. That’s when I – that’s why I played with them a few times.

ctx.x: Yeah. The orchestras were not in any wise integrated at that time. I used to get some calls when the Philharmonic used to do concerts up at Lewisohn Stadium [in Harlem]. They called it the Lewisohn Stadium Orchestra. I used to on occasion get calls to sub with them there. But by the time I got those calls, I was doing Voice of Firestone for ABC on Sundays at the same time. But I still got calls several times, and I was never able to do it. Then when [Pierre] Boulez was with the Philharmonic, and André
Kastelanetz, and Jimmy Holmes was – Jimmy Chambers, rather, was the contractor, he called me for a few things. That’s when I – that’s why I played with them a few times.
What was that like, to finally realize that dream of playing with them?
